title: Socket-neutral Storage Fabric admission over XTP and ordinary sockets
summary: A named XTP service is a transport admission selection, not storage authority or proof of authenticated peer identity. Registered service operations cannot downgrade to ungoverned ordinary sockets after denial.
invariants: StorageRef, virtual namespace, content digest and durable placement remain independent of physical routes and Socket Provider.
Ordinary TCP/IP, Unix sockets and QueueRexx remain first-class for operations that have no named-service binding.

When advanced registration is configured, Service Descriptor Registry chooses canonical service, logical route peer and operational class normal.storage. Storage must never infer these from IP or an unauthenticated request.
XTP FIRST chooses the service before establishing a context; later KEY dispatch must preserve the admitted service and independently authenticated transport peer.
Bound operations require an admitted named context with matching service and independently authenticated peer identity. An absent, denied or mismatched context fails closed.
A service admission is NOT a Storage Fabric read/write/delete authorisation. Peer access control, object identity and replication policy are checked separately.
Capacity governor enforcement is mandatory when operational policy limits per-context rate, aggregate rate or parallel receiver contexts.
Multicast gives untrusted digest-only hints, not HAVE evidence. Read/repair still uses authenticated peer checks and full digest verification.
A verified second copy in Azure Git and a permanent local copy are independently accounted for; an unavailable, unsafe or unverified location does not satisfy durability.
Live ED209 L2/proto36/UDP session admission, persistent KEY and WAN transfer remain unqualified until exercised end-to-end.

Storage repair consumes MU/MI networking through a verified materialisation resolver: networking returns exact locally staged StorageRef bytes plus verification evidence and does not choose or admit the repair destination.
Named Storage service carrier selection remains below repair policy; no IP, UDP port, raw protocol or TAP identity belongs in the repair destination planner.

StoragePeerClient/StoragePeerMaterialiser are the repair source data-plane seam. The network transport behind StoragePeerClient may be XTP named-service networking without exposing carrier details to repair policy.
Successful peer materialisation is temporary verified source evidence only; it does not itself become a durable replica.
procedure: Select ordinary Socket Provider for unbound operations, or resolve a canonical named service and planner rule for bound operations.
Reject a bound operation when the accepting context lacks name/admission/peer evidence; reject mismatches without socket downgrade.
Delegate authorised StorageRef operation to existing StoragePeerService and retain COPY→VERIFY→COMMIT semantics.
Qualify operational caps, authenticated resume, restart persistence, multicast hints and live-grid paths before production.
